title: no-host-namespaces
description: >-
  pid: host, ipc: host, uts: host, cgroup: host and userns_mode: host share the host's namespaces with a Compose service. What each one exposes and what to set instead.
---

Linux gives each container its own view of process IDs, shared memory, the hostname, control groups and user IDs. Compose lets a service drop any of these views and use the host's instead, with `pid: host`, `ipc: host`, `uts: host`, `cgroup: host` or `userns_mode: host`. It usually enters a file to make one tool work, such as a profiler that needs to see host processes or a training job that ran out of shared memory, and then stays. This rule reports each of those keys when it is set to `host`, one finding per key.

- **`pid: host`** lets the container see and signal every process on the host.
- **`ipc: host`** shares the host's shared memory and message queues with the container.
- **`uts: host`** shares the host's hostname and domain name.
- **`cgroup: host`** shows the container the host's whole cgroup tree instead of its own.
- **`userns_mode: host`** turns off user namespace remapping for the container, so root in the container is root on the host.

`pid: service:db` and `ipc: service:db` share a namespace with another service, not with the host, and the rule does not report them. `network_mode: host` is not reported here because it is common and often correct.

## What the rule catches

```yaml title="compose.yaml — the host's process and IPC namespaces"
services:
  agent:
    image: my-agent:1.2.0
    pid: host
    ipc: host
```

Scanning this file reports:

```text
⚠ WARN [docker-doctor/no-host-namespaces]
  Service 'agent' sets 'pid: host', so the container can see and signal every process on the host.
```

## Why it matters

Namespaces are what make a container's view of the machine smaller than the machine. A service that shares the host's PID namespace can inspect every process and its open files and signal them. One that shares the IPC namespace can read the shared memory of host processes. These settings also decide how far a container escape bug goes. In November 2025 runc fixed three escapes, [CVE-2025-31133](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/security/advisories/GHSA-9493-h29p-rfm2), [CVE-2025-52565](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/security/advisories/GHSA-qw9x-cqr3-wc7r) and [CVE-2025-52881](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/security/advisories/GHSA-cgrx-mc8f-2prm). The advisories for the first two strongly recommend user namespaces, with the host's root user not mapped into the container, because that blocks most of the serious parts of the attacks. `userns_mode: host` opts a service out of that protection.

## How to fix it

Remove the key so the service gets its own namespace. If `ipc: host` is there for shared memory, as PyTorch and vLLM often need, set `shm_size` instead.

```yaml title="compose.yaml — shared memory sized, no host namespace"
services:
  inference:
    image: my-inference:1.2.0
    shm_size: 2gb
    pid: service:gateway
  gateway:
    image: my-gateway:1.2.0
```

Remove the key unless the service cannot work without it:

- **Shared memory for PyTorch, vLLM and similar tools**: set `shm_size` on the service. This is the usual reason `ipc: host` is added, and a sized `/dev/shm` does the same job without sharing the host's IPC.
- **A profiler or debugger that must see another process**: share the namespace with that one service using `pid: service:name`, or run the tool on the host.
- **Rootless or remapped containers**: leave `userns_mode` unset so the daemon's remapping applies.

Host monitoring agents, such as a node exporter that reads host process data, legitimately set `pid: host`. Set this rule to `off` in `docker-doctor.config.json` for a project that exists to run such a tool.

## Rule details

- **Rule key** — `docker-doctor/no-host-namespaces`
- **Category** — Compose
- **Default severity** — `warning`
- **Applies to** — Docker Compose files

Explain this rule from the CLI:

```bash
npx @docker-doctor/cli@latest rules explain docker-doctor/no-host-namespaces
```

Change its severity — or turn it off — in your [config file](/docs/reference/configuration):

```ts
// docker-doctor.config.ts
export default {
  rules: {
    "docker-doctor/no-host-namespaces": "off",
  },
};
```

Severity affects the [health score](/docs/reference/scoring): `error` findings cost more points than `warning`, and `info` costs the least.
